Alex: Quick heads-up — ran into a runbook gap during the EU tenant chaos test. active/active failover + residency flags got us into a bad state.
Morgan: what happened exactly?
Alex: We had two regions up (eu-west, us-central). traffic routed to eu-west normally, but during a transient partition eu-west returned 503s. Proxy fallback sent traffic to us-central which accepted writes — tenant had "eu-only" residency in control plane but the proxy didn’t enforce it on fallback.
Priya: oof. so control plane and proxy contract mismatch. Did the write actually persist in us-central DB?
Alex: yes, short-lived. We rolled back via sweep, but the smoke failed for a few minutes and ops had to quarantine that tenant.
Dan: sounds like two separate issues: 1) proxy routing fallback logic needs residency-awareness, 2) control plane should have a stronger residency assertion that data-plane can trust.
Priya: Agreed. My proposal: add a lightweight header the control plane sets on allocation and the proxy insists on when routing/failing over. something like:
```
X-Residency: eu
X-Residency-Assert: true
X-Residency-TTL: 300
```
If header present and region mismatch, proxy must reject fallback and return 429/451 depending on policy.
Morgan: +1 for header. Also need a clear operator path: when proxy rejects, there should be an automated admission for a scoped manual override (with audit) so we don't cause outages for customers during coord work.
Dan: manual override scares me but can be scoped to support with 2FA and a short TTL. We should never let an automated fallback silently violate residency.
Lina: deploy-bot: canary for residency-guard middleware passed in staging at 2026-03-22T18:12Z :white_check_mark:
Alex: Good catch about operator flows. Another edge: KV prefix caching — if eu proxy cached a prefix and then is drained, us-central cache might not have that prefix but will serve writes. We need cache eviction/priming rules tied to residency header.
Priya: long-term, we should refactor the routing code to introduce a ResidencyDecision interface: returns {allowed: bool, reason: string, action: enum} so both proxy and control plane use same logic library. That removes duplication and helps tests.
Morgan: yes — plus a fallback simulator (small harness) to verify for each tenant the routing decisions under partitions. add to CI.
Dan: ops runbook changes (action items):
- detect residency header mismatch alert
- auto-quarantine tenant on cross-region-write attempt
- notify oncall + create incident stub with tenant id
- manual override procedure with audit link
Alex: I'll draft a short RFC for "residency-guard middleware" and the ResidencyDecision interface. Priya, can you prototype the header enforcement in the proxy for a canary?
Priya: I can spike it this week, will push PR to eng-runtime and wire tests.
Morgan: I'll update the runbook draft with the operator steps and add the simulator task to CI backlog.
Dan: who owns the incident template?
Alex: Ops (Dan) — please put a skeleton in the runbook doc and I'll link from RFC.
Dan: done, added placeholder and runbook play steps.
Alex: Great. Let's aim to land the proxy canary + runbook edits before the next oncall rotation. Assigning tentative due date: 2026-03-28.
Morgan: noted. @Priya @Dan please sync tomorrow 10am PT. :calendar:
Priya: ack.
